This page explains archive workflows. It is not a substitute for Spotify, Apple Podcasts, or other platform account support.

Fix it fast

Common issues and what to do next

Each path below points to a real archive workflow instead of a dead-end support loop.

A listen link failed

Start with the show page, then use the correction flow if the archive route is the problem.

  • Open the show page and try another listen or official link first.
  • If every archive link is wrong, send a correction with the broken destination and the correct URL.
  • If Spotify, Apple Podcasts, or another platform itself is down, use that platform’s support.
Report a broken link

I cannot find a show

Search is broader than title-only matching, and some misses are better solved through collections or creator names.

  • Try the exact title, then creator, then a key tag or tonal phrase.
  • Browse related collections if you only remember the vibe, format, or runtime.
  • If the show is missing entirely, use the new-show submission path.
Submit a missing show

My filters returned nothing

Most empty states come from stacking too many narrow constraints at once.

  • Remove filters one at a time until results reappear.
  • Switch from exact genre labels to broader tags, tones, or completion status.
  • Use collections when you want a recommendation path rather than a strict filter set.
Open collections

A page has wrong metadata

Objective facts can be fixed even when editorial review or ratings remain unchanged.

  • Use the correction path for links, creators, status, credits, episode counts, and similar factual fields.
  • Add a source when you can so the archive can verify the change faster.
  • Use creator verification when you are the official source or representative.
Start a correction

My rating did not stick

Community ratings are anonymous, but they still rely on a browser-scoped token so one device keeps one active vote per show.

  • Make sure the browser is not blocking the archive’s rating cookie.
  • Vote again from the same device if you meant to update your score.
  • Read the cookies page if you want the exact storage behavior.
Read rating cookie details

The archive chat forgot me

Ask the Archivist keeps recent conversation history only for the current browser session.

  • Refreshing the page usually keeps the current session conversation.
  • Closing the session or clearing site data removes that local memory.
  • Privacy and cookies pages explain what is stored and why.
Read privacy summary
Use the archive better

Better discovery, with less guesswork

The archive works best when you move through it by fit, not just by title memory.

Search beyond title

Try creator names, tonal phrases, status labels, and a few broad tags when the exact title is fuzzy.

Use collections as routes

Collections are listening paths based on mood, tone, or use case, not generic folders. They are often the fastest way to recover momentum.

Show pages carry depth

When a card gets you close, open the show page for full description, similar shows, runtime context, official links, and corrections.

Ask the Archivist for route help

The chat is useful when you know what you want but not where it lives. Ask about a show, a rating meaning, or the right correction path.

Trust guide

Ratings and trust signals mean different things on purpose

The archive separates editorial judgment, listener response, and factual verification so one signal does not pretend to be all of them.

Archive Rating

An editorial score based on storytelling, sound, originality, production, and staying power.

Community Rating

Anonymous listener response that reflects real enjoyment and recommendation fit without replacing editorial judgment.

Creator Verified

A factual trust flag for metadata confirmation. It does not mean creator approval of reviews, ratings, or archive placement.

Money, support, creator verification, and outside relationships do not change Archive Rating, Community Rating, or collection placement.

FAQ

Short answers for the questions that come up most often while using the archive.

It means the archive has official or representative proof for objective metadata such as links, credits, release status, or episode details.

It does not mean the creator approved a review, a rating, or a collection decision.

The archive is curated and still growing. A missing show may not have been submitted yet, may still be under review, or may not have enough verified metadata to publish confidently.

If it belongs here, use the new-show submission path instead of waiting for it to appear on its own.

Yes. The correction workflow is designed for guest submissions. Provide the factual issue, the corrected information, and a source when possible.

Nothing auto-publishes. Corrections are reviewed before they change the archive.

The archive is real but still expanding. Some shows already have full reviews, collection appearances, or deeper notes, while others are still indexed more lightly.

That difference reflects current editorial coverage, not sponsorship or paid placement.

No. The archive can help with its own links, metadata, and discovery routes, but it cannot diagnose external platform playback, billing, login, or app-account issues.

Use the platform’s own support if the app is the problem. Use the archive correction path only if the outgoing link here is wrong.

The chat keeps recent history in browser session storage, so closing the session or clearing site data removes it.

If you want the exact storage details, the cookies and privacy pages document the current implementation directly.

Browser behavior

What the site stores, and what it does not

The current public archive keeps the data footprint small and documents the live behavior rather than hiding it behind generic policy text.

  • Ask the Archivist keeps recent conversation history in session storage for the current browser session.
  • Community ratings use an anonymous browser token so one device can update or remove its own rating later.
  • Public browsing does not currently depend on ad-tech or analytics scripts.
  • Privacy and cookie pages exist so you can check the exact current behavior when you need it.
Right route

Use the archive workflow that matches the problem

Discovery issue, factual correction, creator verification, or collection browsing each have their own clean path so you do not have to guess.
